name: Spotify
summary: Registering the app is instant, but Spotify has effectively closed general access: Development Mode allows 5 users per app (and the owner needs Premium), and Extended Quota is only for registered organizations with ~250k MAU. For most agents, plan to stay at 5 users.

composio.note: Composio lists this toolkit but you must bring your own OAuth app (client ID + secret) in a custom auth config.

capabilities.label: Read/control playback for you + 4 others
capabilities.why: Development Mode: 5 allow-listed users per app; the owner needs Premium

capabilities.label: Any Spotify user can connect
capabilities.why: Extended Quota: organizations only, launched service, ~250k MAU

steps.title: Make sure the app owner has Spotify Premium
steps.detail: Since Feb/Mar 2026, Development Mode apps stop working if the owner's Premium lapses.
steps.human: Keep Premium active on the owner account

steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Dashboard
steps.detail: Dashboard → Create app. Name and description appear on the consent screen. Add redirect URIs (Composio BYO: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback). You can have up to 25 client IDs, which share one quota.
steps.agent: Fill in the redirect URIs and choose Web API
steps.human: Accept the Developer Terms and create the app

steps.title: Allow-list your 5 users
steps.detail: Add each user's Spotify email under User Management. Anyone else gets an error at sign-in.
steps.agent: Explain the limit to users in your onboarding

steps.title: Apply for Extended Quota (organizations only)
steps.detail: Use the form from a company email. Criteria: a legally registered business, an active launched service, about 250k MAU, and availability in key Spotify markets.
steps.agent: Draft the application and a compliance checklist against the Developer Terms

launchToday: Ship to yourself plus 4 testers in Development Mode today.
Composio has no managed Spotify app. You need your own client ID.
If you need the public, treat Spotify as partner-only and design around it.
rejections: Applying as an individual (Extended Quota has been organizations-only since May 15, 2025)
Below the ~250k MAU bar or not yet launched
Use cases Spotify reviewers flag as not driving artist discovery or as automation risk

blockers.fix: Development Mode caps you at 5 allow-listed users per app. There's no self-serve way around it.
All your Development Mode client IDs share one quota since July 2026. Cache and batch calls.
The owner's Premium subscription lapsed. Renew it.

uncertain: Spotify doesn't publish Extended Quota review times.
The ~250k MAU threshold comes from Spotify's 2025 criteria. Agencies may be judged differently.

name: Zoom
summary: An unpublished General app works only for users in your own Zoom account. To let other accounts connect, the app has to pass Marketplace review (functional, then security), or get approval to share a beta link, which needs SAST/DAST evidence. Expect weeks, and few apps pass on the first try.

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app, so you can ship without registering your own. Bring your own app for your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes, or your own rate limits.

capabilities.label: Your own account's meetings & recordings
capabilities.why: Unpublished apps work for users in your Zoom account without review

capabilities.label: Other companies' users connect
capabilities.why: Marketplace review: functional + security review; scopes are justified individually

steps.title: Create a General app
steps.detail: Marketplace → Develop → Build App → General app. Choose user-managed (each user authorizes) or admin-managed (account-wide).
steps.agent: Recommend user- vs admin-managed from your scopes
steps.human: Create it while signed in to the Zoom developer account

steps.title: Add scopes with a justification for each
steps.detail: Each scope is a request to Zoom's Security Review team, which rejects anything that isn't needed. Add the OAuth redirect URL (Composio BYO: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) and allow-list it.
steps.agent: Choose the minimal granular scopes and write a justification for each

steps.title: Verify your domains
steps.detail: Privacy policy, terms, redirect, webhook and home URLs must all be on domains you verify in the build flow.
steps.agent: Produce the verification records

steps.title: Prepare the security documentation
steps.detail: SSDLC doc, SAST and DAST scan output (real scanner output, not summaries), privacy policy, plus 3 of: pentest summary, security policy, incident response, vulnerability management, dependency policy. TLS 1.2+.
steps.agent: Run SAST/DAST scans and draft the policies
steps.human: Approve the policies and commission a pentest if needed

steps.title: Submit for review (functional → security)
steps.detail: Give test account credentials and reviewer notes. Zoom says few apps pass on the first attempt.
steps.agent: Write the reviewer notes and test plan

launchToday: Composio-managed Zoom auth lets external users connect today.
Build and dogfood inside your own Zoom account. No review needed.
Start the security pack (SAST/DAST, policies) now. It's the long pole.
rejections: Scopes broader than the feature needs
Scan evidence submitted as written summaries, not scanner output
Redirect or webhook URLs on unverified domains
No working test account for the reviewer

blockers.problem: Users from another company get an error installing
blockers.fix: The app is unpublished. Publish it (or get beta sharing approved) through review, or use Composio-managed auth meanwhile.

blockers.problem: Account admin must approve the app
blockers.fix: Many accounts require admin pre-approval in Marketplace settings. Send the admin your listing link.

uncertain: Zoom doesn't publish review turnaround. 2–6 weeks is an estimate from developer reports.

name: Shopify
summary: Custom distribution (one store, or stores in one Plus org) needs no review. Public distribution means App Store review, a one-time registration fee, and a separate review to access protected customer data such as names and emails. Your distribution choice is permanent.

composio.note: Composio lists this toolkit but you must bring your own OAuth app (client ID + secret) in a custom auth config.

capabilities.label: Connect one merchant's store
capabilities.why: Custom distribution: install link, no App Store review

capabilities.label: Any merchant can install
capabilities.why: Public distribution requires App Store review

capabilities.label: Read customer names, emails, addresses
capabilities.why: Protected customer data: level 1/2 access needs its own review for public apps

steps.title: Create a Partner organization and the app
steps.detail: Create it in the Dev Dashboard with the Shopify CLI. Add redirect URLs (Composio BYO: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).
steps.agent: Scaffold with the Shopify CLI and set scopes and redirects
steps.human: Sign up for the Partner org

steps.title: Choose the distribution method (permanent)
steps.detail: Custom (one store or one Plus org) or Public (App Store). **You can't change it later.** If you have separate dev and prod apps, choose on the prod app.
steps.agent: Lay out the trade-offs

steps.title: Request protected customer data access
steps.detail: Declare which fields you need and why, and meet the level 1 (or level 2) requirements. Until it's approved, the API won't return that data from non-dev stores.
steps.agent: Draft the data-use justification and implement the requirements (encryption, retention)

steps.title: Register for the App Store and build the listing
steps.detail: One-time registration fee. You need the listing, an app icon, compliance webhooks, and billing via Shopify App Pricing if you charge.
steps.agent: Subscribe the compliance webhooks; draft the listing; run Shopify's AI self-review

steps.title: Submit for App Store review
steps.detail: Status moves Draft → Submitted → Reviewed → Published. If core requirements fail, the app goes to Paused.
steps.agent: Pre-check against the requirements list

launchToday: Use custom distribution for your first merchant today: install link, no review.
Composio has no managed Shopify app (bring your own).
File the protected customer data request early if you need customer PII.
rejections: Requesting access scopes you can't justify
Missing compliance webhooks
Submitting a beta or incomplete app
Billing outside Shopify App Pricing for public apps

blockers.problem: API returns null for customer fields
blockers.fix: You don't have protected customer data access yet. Request it in the dashboard. Development stores work without it.

blockers.problem: “App not found” when connecting via Composio
blockers.fix: Check the store's myshopify domain and that your app's distribution allows that store.

uncertain: The discovery probe found accounts.shopify.com, which is Shopify's own identity service. App OAuth runs per store at https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize, which has no discovery document.
Shopify doesn't state the review turnaround on the cited pages. The ranges are estimates.
The exact registration fee isn't on the cited pages.

name: Calendly
summary: No review gate: a Production OAuth app works for any Calendly user the moment you create it. Two gotchas: each app takes exactly one redirect URI, and new apps get no API access until you pick scopes.
appType: OAuth app (OAuth 2.1, PKCE), Sandbox or Production

composio.note: Composio's managed app lets users connect today. Bring your own for your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes or your own rate limits.

capabilities.label: Read meetings & availability
capabilities.why: Pick the scopes when you create the app; no review

capabilities.label: Book, cancel & share links
capabilities.why: Write scopes include the matching read scope; no review

capabilities.label: Real-time webhooks
capabilities.why: Needs the related read scopes to receive payloads

steps.title: Create a Calendly developer account
steps.detail: Sign up on developer.calendly.com with GitHub or Google. It is **separate from your Calendly user account**.

steps.title: Create a Sandbox app for development
steps.detail: OAuth apps → Create OAuth app → Environment: Sandbox. Sandbox allows `http://localhost` redirect URIs.
steps.agent: Pick the minimal scopes and wire up PKCE locally

steps.title: Choose scopes up front
steps.detail: New apps get **no API access** until scopes are selected. Request the minimum; adding scopes later means users must re-authorize.
steps.agent: Map each agent feature to the scope catalog

steps.title: Create a separate Production app
steps.detail: Production requires https and accepts **exactly one redirect URI**, so use one app for Composio BYO (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) and another for your own callback.
steps.agent: Prepare both app configs
steps.human: Create them and store the secrets

steps.title: Handle tokens the Calendly way
steps.detail: Access tokens last 2 hours; refresh tokens don't expire until used (store the new one every time); max 8 token requests per user per minute.
steps.agent: Implement refresh with single-use refresh tokens and backoff

launchToday: Or create your Production app today: there is no approval queue.
rejections: No review exists, so failures show up at runtime: redirect_uri mismatch (one URI per app)
403 missing scope: the app was created without the scope the endpoint needs

blockers.fix: The token lacks a scope. Add it to the app and send the user through OAuth again.
Refresh tokens are single-use. Persist the new refresh token from every refresh response.
Production apps take one redirect URI. Create a second app.

uncertain: Calendly's docs describe no review gate for Production apps. That is confirmed by its absence, not by an explicit statement.
Whether webhook delivery depends on the end user's Calendly plan isn't stated on the pages read.

name: Dropbox
summary: Works right away in Development status, but a clock starts at 50 linked users: you then have two weeks to win Production approval or new links freeze. Review checks least-privilege permissions, branding and a privacy policy; Dropbox says it answers nearly all requests within a few business days.
appType: Scoped-access app (App folder or Full Dropbox)

composio.note: Composio's managed app lets users connect today. Bring your own for your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes or your own rate limits.

capabilities.label: Read & write files, first 50 users
capabilities.why: Development status: works like production, review not needed below 50 linked users

capabilities.label: Any Dropbox user can connect
capabilities.why: Production approval required once you pass 50 linked users (hard cap 500 in development)

capabilities.label: Access the whole Dropbox, not one folder
capabilities.why: Reviewers check the permission isn't broader than the feature needs

steps.title: Create a scoped app in the App Console
steps.detail: Choose **App folder** unless the agent truly needs the whole Dropbox: reviewers reject broader access than the features need.
steps.agent: Recommend App folder vs Full Dropbox from your features

steps.title: Set permissions and redirect URIs
steps.detail: Permissions tab: tick only the scopes you use. Settings: add redirect URIs (Composio BYO: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).
steps.agent: Configure scopes and test the OAuth flow with PKCE

steps.title: Fix branding and publish an app-specific privacy policy
steps.detail: Follow the developer branding guidelines (don't lead your name with "Dropbox") and say what the app will and won't do with user data.
steps.agent: Draft the privacy policy and check names/logos against the guidelines

steps.title: Reach 50 linked users
steps.detail: You can apply any time, but Dropbox won't review until 50 users are linked. From the 50th link you have **two weeks** before new links freeze.
steps.agent: Draft the beta invite

steps.title: Apply for production status
steps.detail: App Console → Apply for production. Explain how the app uses the API, upload an icon, and mention planned features that justify broader permissions.
steps.agent: Write the application text and permission justifications

launchToday: Your own app serves 50 users with no review. Submit the production application early so the 2-week clock never bites.
rejections: Requests Full Dropbox when an App folder would do
Breaks the branding guidelines (e.g. app name starting with Dropbox)
No app-specific privacy policy
App type on Dropbox's not-allowed list

blockers.fix: You passed 50 users without production approval inside two weeks. Apply (or follow up on the pending request); links resume once approved.

blockers.problem: Need to rename the app after approval
blockers.fix: Production apps can't be renamed by you. Open an API support ticket.

uncertain: "A few business days" is Dropbox's own statement; we haven't measured it.
Team (Business API) apps have separate development limits that the cited guide doesn't cover in detail.

name: Docusign
summary: Building is free in the developer sandbox; going live needs a paid production Docusign account. The old 20-API-call rule is gone: Go-Live runs automatic checks and eligible apps are promoted instantly. Public apps need the Partner Program. Composio has no managed Docusign app.

composio.note: Composio lists this toolkit but you must bring your own OAuth app.

capabilities.label: Send test envelopes (sandbox)
capabilities.why: Free developer account; envelopes aren't legally binding

capabilities.label: Send real envelopes for your company's users
capabilities.why: Go-Live needs a paid production account; promotion is often automatic

capabilities.label: Public app for other Docusign customers
capabilities.why: The 'Public integration' classification requires joining the Partner Program

steps.title: Create a free developer account
steps.detail: Sandbox at account-d.docusign.com, API base demo.docusign.net.

steps.title: Create the integration key
steps.detail: Apps & Keys → Add app: Authorization Code Grant, secret, redirect URI (Composio BYO: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).
steps.agent: Prepare the settings and test consent in the sandbox

steps.title: Build against the sandbox the production way
steps.detail: Read each user's `base_uri` from /oauth/userinfo once and cache it; production hosts differ per data centre. Use webhooks, not polling.
steps.agent: Implement OAuth, base_uri discovery and Connect webhooks

steps.title: Get a paid production account with admin access
steps.detail: Trial plans aren't eligible. ISV partners can apply for a free management account.
steps.human: Buy or pick a supported plan; make sure you're an admin

steps.title: Choose the integration classification
steps.detail: Private custom, third-party key, public (Partner Program) or embedded (ISV Embed licence). It also decides how envelopes are billed.
steps.agent: Recommend the classification from your business model

steps.title: Join the Docusign Partner Program
steps.detail: Required for a public integration that other companies authorize with their own accounts.

steps.title: Run Go-Live
steps.detail: Pick the production account. Eligible apps go live instantly; others go to Pending approval. "Verification required" means the account admin must verify their identity once.
steps.agent: Pre-check eligibility and draft the review notes
steps.human: Start Go-Live and complete identity verification

steps.title: Re-enter secrets and redirect URIs in production
steps.detail: The key is copied to production, but secrets and redirect URIs are not.
steps.agent: Script the production config and switch base URIs

launchToday: Composio can't host this one: bring your own integration key.
If you already have a paid Docusign account, Go-Live can be same-day.
rejections: Trying to go live from a trial plan
Admin identity verification not completed (status: Declined, Verification required)
Wrong classification for the business model
API rule or resource-limit violations such as polling

blockers.problem: Production calls fail right after Go-Live
blockers.fix: Secrets and redirect URIs aren't copied with the key. Add them in production and use the account's base_uri.
The production account admin completes the one-time identity verification, then re-select the Go-Live account.

uncertain: Docusign doesn't say which integrations are auto-promoted vs reviewed, or how long a manual review takes (0–5 days is our estimate).
Partner Program approval time isn't published.
